title: 🎮 Game Making for Kids
description:
Registration for this event is required through the Library.
[Register Here!](https://sandiego.librarymarket.com/event/game-making-kids-494573)

Give your child the thrill of making their very first video game! In this free, one-hour event, kids in grades 3 through 8 will work alongside a live instructor to design a main character, add movement, and create simple challenges--then watch their game come to life. It’s a fun, beginner-friendly way to spark creativity, build problem-solving skills, and get them excited about technology. Presented by [The League of Amazing Programmers](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.jointheleague.org/l/tech-club__;!!OBed2aHXvKmHymw!0-nR1sEeUz174TMjTbPSITQ98pLxU7L4pEjB5GMwgr_BPek04u4JcsLMWoJ49NU5Di4GmR1se7xsitZoqDHBoiFQgGBaoMs$)! Registration is required.

Optionally, if your child wants to save their work, they will need to use Google, Microsoft, or Clever at the beginning of class to login to this website: [https://arcade.makecode.com/](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/arcade.makecode.com/__;!!OBed2aHXvKmHymw!0-nR1sEeUz174TMjTbPSITQ98pLxU7L4pEjB5GMwgr_BPek04u4JcsLMWoJ49NU5Di4GmR1se7xsitZoqDHBoiFQIf2QY-0$)

title: 🤖 Robot Riot - Play and Code
description:
**Play and Learn, It's going to be a Riot!**

This course is curated for kids and teens in grades 3+

Come check out our Brand New Robot Riot, it's a fun way to learn computer science. Kids will race, crash, and have some fun competitions with robots all while learning how it all works!

Younger students can drive the robots and learn some basic programming, while older students can get into the details of the communication protocols and control systems. No experience is necessary.

title: 🧠 AI Agents: License to Code
description:
**This event is tailored to kids and teens grades 5 through 12**

Learn to build interactive games and web applications by collaborating with AI coding agents. This hands-on course teaches you to direct, understand, and refine AI-generated code while creating real projects you can share and use.

**A New Way to Code**
Instead of memorizing syntax or struggling through documentation, you'll learn to partner with Claude Code and other AI agents to bring your ideas to life. Describe what you want, guide the AI, understand what it creates, and refine the results into polished projects. It's like having a senior developer pair programming with you from day one.

title: 🤖 Robo Battles: A LEGO® Robotics Competition
description:
Registration is Required through the library.

Contact:
Email: [mjeffery@sandiego.gov](mailto:mjeffery@sandiego.gov)
Phone Number: [(858) 573-5007](tel:8585735007)

Once the Library has updated their registration page this post will be updated with the link.

**For rising 2nd-6th graders!**

Robo Battles is a LEGO® robotics competition and roleplaying game. Working in pairs, participants will build amazing LEGO® contraptions, create their own characters, and compete in real battles against friends and in tournaments. This hands-on learning experience feels like playing a video game in real life and engages students of all backgrounds and interests. Robo Battles is a free robotics program from the [Grant Imahara STEAM Foundation](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.grantimaharafoundation.org/__;!!OBed2aHXvKmHymw!0Ci9Rd_JbCgvgzNopH6LZKjMSbBo7Cl6RqzQXEDFadRAm0oPRtt3dRSrZG8B8dLc_DyxCYwLc2dLqxuIgivpKld2RA_TBak$), hosted and in partnership with [The League of Amazing Programmers](https://www.jointheleague.org/)

title: Robot Garage:  Programming, 3d Printing and ROBOTS
description:
Visit the Robot Garage and learn something new about programming, robotics or electronics. In the Robot Garage we beta test ideas for new classes, work on personal projects, build circuits, weld and solder, and sometimes run a science experiment.

**These sessions are for students 12 to 18 years old.** Adults are welcome, especially if you'd got technical skills and would like to volunteer to help, but otherwise bring a kid.

Most days we have students building robots with Lego Technics and Micro:bit controllers, but we also use Arduino and Raspberry Pi. Common projects include mobile robots and small robot arms and soldering electronic circuits. Stuck on an Arduino project or a Hack Pack? Bring it with you and let's get it working.

[ *Scouts! Our Lead Instructor is BSA registered and a Merit Badge Counselor: Contact us if you'd like to run a session as a patrol event or have 3-5 Scouts who want to complete their Programming, Electronics or Robotics merit badges.* ]

title: Coding for Kids and Teens
description:
You Must Register through the Library:
[Sign Up Link](https://sandiego.librarymarket.com/event/intro-python-programming-453645)

Join us for an exciting free one-hour Coding class at The LEAGUE of Amazing Programmers, tailored specifically for students in 4th to 12th grade. This special event is designed to give learners a smooth introduction to the engaging world of coding by engaging them in the fundamentals while creating thoughtful designs.

**Event Highlights:**

1. Hands-On Coding: Watch as your child dives into the world of programming with Python, one of the most versatile and beginner-friendly languages. Under the guidance of our experienced instructors, they'll learn the basics of coding while creating fun and interactive games.
2. Engaging Curriculum: Our curriculum is carefully crafted to make learning coding enjoyable and accessible for students of all skill levels. From understanding fundamental concepts to building their own games, your child will embark on an exciting coding journey.

Don't miss this chance to spark your child's curiosity and creativity through coding! RSVP now and let's embark on an exciting coding adventure together. Limited spots available, so secure your spot today!

title: CS Higher Education & Careers - Info and Q/A for Parents & HS Students
description:
If your teen is interested in coding and computer science, we welcome you to join this discussion lead by the Executive Director of the LEAGUE of Amazing Programmers, a San Diego-based nonprofit organization focused on coding education for youth. Teens and parents who'd like to learn about higher education pathways and computer science career options will get to hear from an expert in the field who will lead an open discussion.

Parents, if your child will also be attending please add them as a guest.

title: Motors Clinic: How to Make Your Robot Move
description:
Learn how to make a robot move! 🕺

Electric motors turn electricity into motion, and they are one of the most important, and most common, devices in the modern world. In this clinic, you will learn about the most common types of motors and how to program a microcontroller to control them.

In this clinic, we will learn about how to control the most common motors in robotics applications: brush motors, hobby servos and stepper motors. We will do basic programming with a block language, so no programming experience is required.

In the class, we will cover:

* Hobby servos, 180 degree position with low grade accuracy
* Steppers, 360 rotation with high accuracy
* Brush motors, continuous motion with no positioning.

Our [curriculum is online](https://league-curriculum.github.io/Motors/) if you'd like a preview.

title: AI Agents: License to Code
description:
**This event is tailored to kids and teens grades 5 through 12**

Learn to build interactive games and web applications by collaborating with AI coding agents. This hands-on course teaches you to direct, understand, and refine AI-generated code while creating real projects you can share and use.

**A New Way to Code**
Instead of memorizing syntax or struggling through documentation, you'll learn to partner with Claude Code and other AI agents to bring your ideas to life. title: Getting Started with Professional C++
description:
Get started with C++ on VSCode with one click.

Compiling a single C++ file is easy, but building a whole C++ project can be hard without the right tools, like Github and CMake. In this session we will get you started with a pre-configured C++ project that you can use to build, test, debug and run your own multi-file C++ projects.

title: Video Game Making for Teens and Kids
description:
This event is catered to teens and kids 5th grade through 12th grade.

Give your child a front-row seat to the exciting world of game creation - taught live by a Professional Developer! In this one-time online event, kids will explore how real games are built using the beginner-friendly Godot engine, a favorite among indie studios worldwide. They’ll create characters, program player movement, spawn enemies, and add the finishing touches that will bring their very own playable game to life. It’s hands-on inspiration that blends creativity, coding, and design - perfect for sparking their imagination and showing them what’s possible in just one session!

Participants will need a Windows, Linux, or Apple computer with access to the internet.

Optionally participants can install the game engine in advance here: [https://godotengine.org/](https://godotengine.org/)
Or participants can use the online editor without the hassle of the installation here: [https://editor.godotengine.org/releases/latest/](https://editor.godotengine.org/releases/latest/)
